effects.name: Rage
effects.notes:
You can imbue yourself with a primal power called Rage, granting extraordinary might and resilience. You can enter a Rage as a Bonus Action if you aren't wearing Heavy armor. You can enter your Rage a number of times equal to the Rages column of the Barbarian Features table. You regain one expended use when you finish a Short Rest and all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

While active, your Rage grants the following benefits:
Damage Resistance. You have Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.
Rage Damage. When you make an attack using Strength with a weapon or an Unarmed Strike and deal damage, you add a bonus that increases as you gain levels.
Strength Advantage. You have Advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws.
No Concentration or Spells. You cannot maintain Concentration or cast spells.

Duration. Rage lasts until the end of your next turn. It ends early if you don Heavy armor or become Incapacitated. On each subsequent turn, you may extend your Rage to the end of your next turn by making an attack roll against an enemy, forcing an enemy to make a saving throw, or taking a Bonus Action to extend your Rage. A Rage can last up to 10 minutes.

effects.name: Unarmored Defense
effects.notes: While you aren't wearing any armor, your base Armor Class equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Constitution modifier. You can use a Shield and still gain this benefit.

effects.name: Weapon Mastery
effects.notes: You can use the mastery properties of two Simple or Martial Melee weapons of your choice. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change one of your chosen weapons. You gain additional mastery choices at higher Barbarian levels.

effects.name: Danger Sense
effects.notes: You have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws against effects you can see. You do not gain this benefit if you are Incapacitated.

effects.name: Reckless Attack
effects.notes: When you make your first attack on your turn, you can attack recklessly, granting Advantage on Strength-based attack rolls until the start of your next turn. Attack rolls against you have Advantage for the same duration.

effects.name: Primal Knowledge
effects.notes: You gain proficiency in one skill of your choice from the Barbarian’s level 1 skill list. In addition, while your Rage is active, you can use Strength for Acrobatics, Intimidation, Perception, Stealth, or Survival checks instead of their normal ability.

effects.name: Ability Score Improvement
effects.notes: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat for which you qualify.

effects.name: Bardic Inspiration
effects.notes:
You can supernaturally inspire others through words, music, or dance. This inspiration is represented by your Bardic Inspiration die, which starts as a d6.

Using Bardic Inspiration. As a Bonus Action, you can inspire a creature within 60 feet of yourself who can see or hear you. That creature gains one Bardic Inspiration die. A creature can have only one Bardic Inspiration die at a time.

Within the next hour, when the creature fails a D20 Test, it can roll the Bardic Inspiration die and add the result to the d20, potentially turning failure into success. The die is expended when rolled.

Number of Uses. You can use Bardic Inspiration a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one) and regain all uses when you finish a Long Rest.

At Higher Levels. The Bardic Inspiration die increases to a d8 at level 5, a d10 at level 10, and a d12 at level 15.

effects.name: Spellcasting
effects.notes:
You have learned to cast spells through your bardic arts.

Cantrips. You know two Bard cantrips of your choice. Dancing Lights and Vicious Mockery are recommended. You learn more cantrips at Bard levels 4 and 10. When you gain a Bard level, you may replace one cantrip you know.

Spell Slots. You use the Bard Features table to determine how many spell slots you have to cast level 1+ spells.

Prepared Spells. You prepare a list of Bard spells equal to the Prepared Spells column of the Bard Features table. Prepared spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

Changing Spells. When you gain a Bard level, you may replace one prepared spell.

Spellcasting Ability. Charisma is your spellcasting ability.

Spellcasting Focus. You may use a Musical Instrument as a Spellcasting Focus.
